chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Take the pebbles of the Jamarah with your left hand, and throw with your right.'

key_terms.حَصَى الْجِمَارِ: Pebbles of the Jamarah (the stone pillars in Mina)

ai.seo_question: How should one hold and throw the pebbles during the stoning of the Jamarah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the specific sunnah of holding the pebbles in the left hand before casting them with the right, a practice widely adopted in Shia fiqh to distinguish it from other rituals. It underscores the meticulous attention to physical detail in the performance of Hajj, reflecting the Imam's guidance on perfecting the outward acts of worship. This instruction is part of the broader legal framework governing the days of Tashreeq, emphasizing both ritual purity and symbolic action.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said,
‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Take a pebble (for pelting the) Jamarah by your left hand, and pelt with your right’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn abu Hamzah from abu Basir who has said the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘You should keep the pebbles to be thrown on al-Jamar in your left hand and throw them with your right hand.’”
